answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a oasis as the anchor of the cost.
